test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following symptoms is related to myopia?

options.text: A person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly.
A person can see both nearby and distant objects distinctly.
A person cannot see both nearby and distant objects distinctly.
A person can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Myopia, also known as nearsightedness, is a common refractive error where distant objects appear blurry while close objects can be seen clearly.
 
• It occurs when the eye's shape causes light rays to bend (refract) incorrectly, focusing images in front of the retina instead of on it.
 
• Myopia is often hereditary and can develop gradually or rapidly, often worsening during childhood and adolescence.
 
• Common symptoms include difficulty seeing distant objects, squinting, eye strain, and headaches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyperopia (Farsightedness)**

 
 
• A condition where distant objects can be seen more clearly than nearby objects.
 
• Occurs when the eyeball is too short or the cornea has too little curvature, causing light to focus behind the retina.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**
 
 
• A common condition where the eye does not focus light evenly onto the retina, leading to blurred or distorted vision.
 
• Usually caused by an irregularly shaped cornea or lens.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• An age-related condition where the eye's lens loses flexibility, making it difficult to focus on close objects.
 
• Typically affects individuals over the age of 40.
 
 
 
• **Corrective Measures for Myopia**
 
 
• Eyeglasses or contact lenses are the most common methods to correct myopia, adjusting the focus directly onto the retina.
 
• Refractive surgery, such as LASIK, can also be an option to permanently reshape the cornea.
